about: ChitBridge compatibility register: every outside system we work with, by service. ONE file, read by the Standards page (Kind = Compatibility) and the Compatibility lab (N04). fit: one-to-one | alongside | gap. status: works | partly | planned. proof: live | stand-in | not-yet (proof_ref names the test or the connector run). A 'works' row always names its proof. pa: the product area (one of STD_PRODUCT_AREAS in app/cap-standards.js). T3-COMPAT (2026-10-14), read by the Standards page's Works with tab: dir = which way it moves — in (into ChitBridge) | out (out to the system) | both; written here by hand, read by stdCompatRows. code = the chitbridge-api file that does the move ('' = not built). test = the chitbridge-api test or stand-in that proves it ('' = none yet; a live proof_ref is then the only proof). Every row has all three; a row with an unknown dir is dropped, not guessed.

rows.service: Products and stock, up to your catalogue
rows.p: Your Tally items and stock appear in your catalogue
rows.proof_ref: TallyPrime run on store tallytest (tools/tally-connector, sync-products · sync-stock)
rows.note: Read from Tally's Stock Item list over its local port; stock read back after a sale.

rows.service: A Sales voucher for every order
rows.p: Every order becomes a Sales voucher in Tally, once
rows.proof_ref: TallyPrime run on store tallytest: Sales voucher read back from Tally
rows.note: Party, sales, bank and cash ledgers are created on first use. Reference CB-<chit>.

rows.service: A Receipt voucher when you mark a bill paid
rows.p: Mark paid, and Tally gets the Receipt against that bill
rows.proof_ref: TallyPrime run on store tallytest: Receipt voucher Agst Ref CB-<chit>
rows.note: A cash sale is already settled, so it books no Receipt.

rows.service: A Purchase voucher on the buyer's side
rows.p: When your supplier completes the order, your Tally gets the Purchase voucher
rows.m: Not yet run against a live Tally
rows.roadmap: Run once on a live Tally with a buyer's connector.

rows.service: Your GSTIN, read from the Tally company
rows.p: Your GSTIN comes from Tally, so you do not type it twice
rows.m: Tally's GST registration master cannot be read safely yet
rows.roadmap: Read the GSTIN that Tally writes on our own posted vouchers instead.

rows.service: Items up; an invoice and a customer payment for every order
rows.p: Zoho Books gets the invoice and the payment for every order
rows.m: A live Zoho organisation run is not recorded yet
rows.roadmap: Record one live run; it may need customer_id or item_id on lines.

rows.p: NetSuite gets your orders and invoices
rows.roadmap: A NetSuite adapter in the same connector (core + one adapter file), proven on a stand-in first.

rows.service: Move your books in from Xero exports
rows.p: Bring a client's Xero chart, contacts, items and balances in from its exports
rows.m: Files only; no live Xero connection
rows.roadmap: Phase 1 is the five exports; a live connection comes after a recorded run with a real practice.

rows.service: An accountant's Xero period beside ours
rows.p: Lay a Xero trial balance, P&L and balance sheet beside ours, line by line
rows.m: Not yet run on a live Xero export
rows.roadmap: Record one run with an Australian practice's own export.

rows.service: An invoice and a payment for every order
rows.p: Xero gets the invoice and the payment for every order
rows.m: No Xero adapter in the connector yet
rows.roadmap: A Xero adapter in the same connector (core + one adapter file), proven on a stand-in first — the Australian launch depends on it.

rows.service: Move your books in from QuickBooks exports
rows.p: Bring a client's QuickBooks chart, contacts, items and balances in from its exports
rows.m: Files only; no live QuickBooks connection
rows.roadmap: Phase 1 is the exports; a live connection comes after a recorded run.

rows.service: Items and stock up, a sales order for every order
rows.p: Your GoFrugal items and stock reach your catalogue; each order becomes a GoFrugal sales order
rows.m: Written from GoFrugal's published API; not yet run on a live GoFrugal server
rows.roadmap: Record one live run on a shop's own GoFrugal server; the first run may correct a field name in the adapter file.

rows.service: An open-network order, read as a chit
rows.p: An order from an open-network buyer app can be read as a chit
rows.proof_ref: chitbridge-api tests/beckn-map.test.js (19 fields seen in a live Beckn 1.1.0 capture)
rows.m: Mapping tested; no route takes a Beckn message yet
rows.roadmap: Beckn-compatible, not ONDC-registered (the recorded decision; see the Beckn and ONDC rows of the register). A route that takes a Beckn order comes when a shop asks for it.

rows.service: Products up, orders and receipts down
rows.p: No accounts software? A spreadsheet works the same way
rows.note: The same connector with the CSV adapter: products.csv in, orders.csv and receipts.csv out.
